title: NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (December 2026) — the residential print with no federal input, 10:00 a.m. ET
source: IR: NAHB's own "2026 HMI Schedule" table at nahb.org/news-and-economics/housing-economics/indices/nahb-wells-fargo-housing-market-index-release-dates, fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 46,943 bytes) — row "Dec. 2026 | December, 16, 2026" under the standing note "Normal release time: 10:00 AM Eastern Time" (the stray comma is NAHB's, transcribed verbatim). Promoted this session from the `EST:` proposal on four checks, all primary: (1) the live table above; (2) the Wayback snapshot 20260824180935 of the same page carrying the identical December row, so the date predates this lane; (3) seven schedule years recovered from the publisher's own page (20201231, 20211021, 20220928, 20231001, 20241225, 20251122, 20260824) giving 84 publisher-authored dates 2020-2026, of which 80 have elapsed and 78 are US trading sessions — an unbroken mid-month convention, and every one of the seven December rows a normal weekday session; (4) NAHB's live HMI page (HTTP 200, 61,320 bytes) reporting "HMI Key Findings: August 2026" — index 35 — the edition its own schedule dates 2026-08-17, so the publisher's calendar and the publisher's output agree. NAHB produces this series; it is not an aggregator. The no-self-confirm limit binds the sweep that discovered this id (nahb-hmi-2026-11-17), not this event's own independent initial research — same precedent as existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 with NAR's calendar. 2026-12-16 is a normal Wednesday session. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: Initial research 2026-09-06 (docs/research/events/nahb-hmi-2026-12-16.md) wrote this canonical file; the id previously existed only as proposals/nahb-hmi-2026-12-16.from-nahb-hmi-2026-11-17.json, which is now inert. Stance: STAND ASIDE on every horizon. The tape channel is measured null and was not re-litigated — the proposing lane settled it (ITB open->close 0.9559% vs 0.9627% on 78 HMI days, p=0.96; paired sentiment-vs-data 35/71 = 49.3%, sign p=1.00), and this session reproduced those cells to four decimals on an independent pull. What this session tested instead is the reason the proposal filed the id: whether a privately produced residential print acquires value when the federal ones go dark, five days after cr-expiry-2026-12-11 (`estimate`, `high`) and one session before the funding-exposed housing-starts-2026-12-17. AVAILABILITY: SUPPORTED, on the record rather than by assertion. Through the 2025-26 lapse, while Census published nothing residential for 114 days, NAHB published October (index 37), November (38), December (39) and January 2026 (37) on its scheduled dates — 4 for 4, verified from Wayback snapshots of NAHB's own HMI page. INFORMATION VALUE: NOT SUPPORTED and not measurable — the blackout contains only three HMI sessions (ITB open->close 0.8530% vs 0.8880% blackout baseline, p=1.00) and n=3 cannot reach p<0.05 by any arrangement; the better-powered regime test is also null (blackout window ITB 0.8705% vs 0.9672%, n=70, p=0.45). THE NOVEL FINDING, and a correction to the corridor's framing: funding immunity is not what decides publication, INPUT independence is. The Federal Reserve is statutorily self-funded and its G.17 still went dark — its own feed carries "G.17 October 17th release delayed", "G.17 November 18th release delayed", September data finally on 2025-12-03 and October+November merged into one 2025-12-23 release. Same defer-and-merge pattern Census showed, from a publisher with no appropriations exposure at all, because G.17's inputs are federal surveys. NAHB surveys its own builder members, which is the actual load-bearing fact. 2026-12-16 is also a stacked HMI+G.17 morning (retail sales 08:30 `confirmed`, industrial production 09:15 `confirmed`, MTIS 10:00 `estimate`) — unusual for a December edition, 1 of 7 historically — so the proposing lane's registered pre-open attribution applies to it. symbols: [] and impact: low re-derived, not inherited; nothing here licenses an entry.
